title: Keller maps injective on integer points
plain: Take a polynomial map of 3-space with integer coefficients whose Jacobian determinant is identically 1 (a Keller map). Prove or disprove: if it never sends two different integer points to the same point, then it is a polynomial automorphism. Caution: if some 3D Keller counterexample with F(0)=0 has only finitely many colliding integer pairs, then F(Nx)/N for suitable N is an integer Keller map injective on Z^3 that is not an automorphism.
math: Let $F\in\mathbb{Z}[x,y,z]^3$ with $\det JF\equiv 1$. Prove or disprove: if $F|_{\mathbb{Z}^3}$ is injective, then $F$ has a polynomial inverse (equivalently, by Bia{\l}ynicki-Birula--Rosenlicht, $F$ is injective on $\mathbb{C}^3$). Caution: if some 3D Keller counterexample with $F(0)=0$ has only finitely many colliding integer pairs, then $F(Nx)/N$ for suitable $N$ is an integer Keller map injective on $\mathbb{Z}^3$ that is not an automorphism.
review_note: Posed as prove-or-disprove: the scaling F(Nx)/N could turn a 3D Keller counterexample with finitely many integer collisions into a refutation.
